prompt:
Create a NEW original ASHVEIL cinder bear WALK atlas in exactly TWO ROWS by TWO COLUMNS, FOUR large separate whole-body bear sprites on transparent RGBA. All four sprites face ONE SAME DIRECTION described below. Do NOT make a 4x4 sheet and do NOT mix viewing angles. This is a 340kg heavy brown grizzly-like quadruped: ash-grey shoulder hump, charcoal-black fur tips over soot-dark brown fur, warm dark-brown broad short muzzle, tiny round ears, black nose, small dark eyes, thick heavy chest and rump, FOUR stout jointed legs with broad clawed paws and a tiny stub tail. Exquisite detailed crisp pixel-art clusters, muted natural materials, consistent elevated three-quarter game camera. No wolf/dog anatomy, armor, accessories, glow, flames, blood, targets, floor, contact shadow, checkerboard, text or grid. True transparent large gutters, every complete silhouette separated and not clipped. Same body/head size in all FOUR poses.

READING ORDER: top-left=A CONTACT, top-right=A PASSING, bottom-left=B OPPOSITE CONTACT, bottom-right=B PASSING. A and B are opposite anatomical foot phases, not duplicate poses or fur shifts. Slow heavy four-beat locomotion with at least two/three paws supporting the bear, never a floating trot or upright bear. Show distinct front AND rear foot changes. The trunk is stable and low, the head remains level/forward, minimal body bounce.

DIRECTION FRONT: all FOUR bears face straight down toward the viewer in the same elevated frontal view, muzzle centered, rump behind. A CONTACT: VIEWER-LEFT front paw is extended far forward/lower with its toes planted, VIEWER-RIGHT front paw tucked back under chest; opposite hind paw ahead behind the foreleg. A PASSING: viewer-left front paw is under chest and viewer-right front paw is visibly lifted/bent, paw sole a little visible; hind feet pass beneath hips. B CONTACT (BOTTOM-LEFT) MUST REVERSE THE SUPPORT: VIEWER-RIGHT front paw is extended far forward/lower with toes planted and VIEWER-LEFT front paw tucked back under chest; opposite hind leg ahead. B PASSING: viewer-right front paw under chest, viewer-left front paw visibly lifted/bent. Bottom-left and top-left must have opposite front paws ahead; this is critical. Never draw three bears with the same viewer-left paw extended.
